title: Mehtab Bagh - The Moonlight Garden Opposite the Taj Mahal
content:
Mehtab Bagh - Agra, 

Mehtab Bagh is a garden steeped in romance, legend, and quiet beauty. It is often known as the “Moonlight Garden” because of the magical way the light of the moon and the setting sun plays across its lawns and casts a shimmering reflection of the Taj Mahal in its waters.

Originally laid out as part of a series of Mughal gardens, Mehtab Bagh gained its fame when Emperor Shah Jahan chose this site as the perfect vantage point to view his beloved Taj Mahal across the river. This garden-as-viewpoint concept gives every visitor a moment of stillness and reflection. Today, the garden’s gentle pathways, grassy lawns, and the quiet river-bank panorama combine to create one of the most serene spots in Agra.

Walking through Mehtab Bagh you feel a different pace of time. Instead of busy crowds, there are quiet benches shaded by trees, distant views of the Taj’s marble gleaming in sunlight, and the chatter of birds near the water’s edge. The garden is especially beloved for sunrise visits when the early light bathes the Taj in soft gold, or for sunset walks when the sky turns pink and the Taj reflects gently across the water.

For photographers and couples, Mehtab Bagh offers a unique experience: views of the Taj Mahal without being inside its hustle - instead, from a calm vantage point across the river, in a green space designed to pause the world. History lovers also enjoy exploring its Mughal-era design: square layout, water-channels, fountains, and the remains of pavilions once built for royal pleasure.

In the monsoon, the Yamuna may swell and parts of the gardens feel the river’s presence strongly - adding a touch of wildness to the otherwise calm setting. During the winter months, the garden is cool, clear and peaceful, making it a top pick for early morning visits.

Visiting Mehtab Bagh is less about rushing through and more about being present. Sit by the river, look across at the Taj Mahal, and let the breeze and view work their magic. It is one of the most poetic places in Agra - where nature, architecture, water and memory meet.

Mehtab Bagh Timings:

Mehtab Bagh is open from sunrise to sunset daily.
The gates open early in the morning and visitors often come before dawn for the first light. It remains open until the late evening, giving ideal sunset and moonlight views of the Taj.

Mehtab Bagh Entry Fee:

The standard entry fee for Mehtab Bagh is modest for Indian nationals, and higher for foreign visitors. Children under age 15 often enter free. For example, official rates list Indian-citizen entry around ₹ 25 - ₹ 30 and foreign visitor entry around ₹ 300. Always check the official ticket counters or websites for the latest rate before visiting.

How to Reach:

Mehtab Bagh is located just across the Yamuna from the Taj Mahal in Agra. From the city centre or from Agra Fort or Taj Mahal complex, one can hire a taxi, e-rickshaw or auto to reach the garden’s entrance. The walk through the garden gives an unobstructed panoramic view of the Taj on the opposite bank. Since it lies in the river-front zone, transport may include crossing a bridge or following riverside roads.

Top Nearby Attractions:

While visiting Mehtab Bagh, it is easy to combine the experience with other Agra highlights. The Taj Mahal is just across the river. The historic Agra Fort lies nearby in the same city. The lesser-known but beautiful Itimad‑ud‑Daulah’s Tomb (often called “Baby Taj”) is also a short drive away. Wandering the old lanes of Tajganj and sampling local Agra sweets completes a perfect half-day outing.

faqs.question: What makes Mehtab Bagh special in Agra?
faqs.answer: Its perfect alignment facing the Taj Mahal and the river-bank view make this garden a unique place for reflection and photography.

faqs.question: Is Mehtab Bagh the same as the Taj Mahal?
faqs.answer: No. Mehtab Bagh is a separate Mughal garden located across the Yamuna that offers a vantage point for viewing the Taj Mahal from the opposite side

faqs.question: What is the best spot inside Mehtab Bagh for viewing the Taj?
faqs.answer: The riverside edge facing the Taj gives unobstructed views and reflections - great around sunrise and sunset.

faqs.question: How much time is needed to explore Mehtab Bagh?
faqs.answer: About 30 to 60 minutes is sufficient for the main garden and views; more time can be spent if relaxing or photographing.

faqs.question: How does Mehtab Bagh compare to other Agra attractions?
faqs.answer: Unlike busy monuments inside fenced areas, Mehtab Bagh offers a calm green space with a panoramic view of the Taj - making it a unique addition to any Agra visit.
